question: During the 2026 New Year’s celebrations, a serious fire broke out in Le Constellation club in the Swiss town of Crans-Montana, resulting in the death of 40 people, mostly very young people, and more than 100 injuries. Among the victims of this very serious accident are a number of EU citizens, including six young Italians.

Upon payment of a CHF 200 000 bond, the Swiss authorities released the owner of the club, Jacques Moretti, despite the very serious charges against him and the risk that he might flee or the evidence might end up contaminated1. In the light of the above: 1.
What view does the Commission take of those facts?
Taking into account that young EU citizens from five countries died, is it considering taking part as a civil party?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2026) The Commission does not comment on ongoing cases. The EU reacted swiftly after the tragic fire in the bar during the New Year's celebrations at the ski resort Crans-Montana.

In response to Switzerland´s request for assistance via the EU Civil Protection Mechanism, the EU coordinated the evacuation of severely injured patients for specialised treatment, with Member States offering hospital capacity and medical transport support.

The EU's Emergency Response Coordination Centre swiftly deployed liaison officers to oversee the medical evacuation and liaise with the Swiss national authorities on-site. As stated by the President of the Commission, the EU stands in full solidarity with Switzerland and with those affected by this tragedy.
The Commission trusts that the Swiss authorities will conduct a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding this tragedy.
